title: India A Declare at 464, Lead New Zealand A by 428 on Day 2
excerpt: Fifties from Jurel, Tilak Varma and Washington Sundar built a commanding total in Lincoln before Prasidh Krishna struck twice on his return from injury.
body:
• India A declared at 464 for 5 on day 2 of the third unofficial Test against New Zealand A at the Bert Sutcliffe Oval in Lincoln, a lead of 428 runs.
  • Dhruv Jurel made 71, Tilak Varma finished unbeaten on 81 and Washington Sundar unbeaten on 50, building on Yashasvi Jaiswal's 102 and Sai Sudharsan's 88.
  • Prasidh Krishna, returning from a left hamstring injury, dismissed both New Zealand A openers to leave the hosts 36 for 2 at stumps.
  • The match continues to day 3 on Monday, with New Zealand A still trailing by 428 runs.

India A tightened their grip on the third unofficial Test against New Zealand A on day 2 in Lincoln, declaring at 464 for 5 and then reducing the hosts to 36 for 2 by stumps at the Bert Sutcliffe Oval on Sunday, November 8 — a lead of 428 runs with two days left.

India A resumed at 227 for 2 and added 237 runs before declaring with about an hour of play left. The total was built across the order rather than by one innings: Yashasvi Jaiswal's 102 off 138 balls on day 1, his second century of the tour, set the platform, and day 2 belonged to the middle order.

Jurel attacks, Tilak and Washington finish

Captain Dhruv Jurel, who resumed on 12, took on the short-pitched bowling early and reached his half-century off 75 balls by clipping a delivery down the leg side for four, according to Cricbuzz. He finished with 71 off 95 balls, with 9 fours and 2 sixes, before he was dismissed.

Sai Sudharsan, resuming on 77, added 11 more before Zak Gibson bowled him for 88, 12 short of a century. Gibson finished with 2 for 73 and was the only New Zealand A bowler with two wickets in the brief scores reported by Cricbuzz and CricTracker.

Ravindra Jadeja chipped in with 25 before edging to first slip. Tilak Varma and Washington Sundar then batted through to the declaration in an unbeaten 114-run partnership, according to both reports. Tilak finished on 81 not out, with 5 fours and 2 sixes in CricTracker's account, and Washington reached 50 not out as India A closed the innings after 146 overs.

Cricbuzz reported New Zealand A's attack was stretched thin: Darun Ferns had trouble with his back and Jarrod McKay, with a side strain, did not bowl at all, forcing the hosts to use nine bowlers.

Prasidh strikes on return

The declaration left New Zealand A a short, difficult session, and Prasidh Krishna made it harder. Returning to the side after recovering from a left hamstring injury, he dismissed both openers — Rhys Mariu was cleaned up for a duck and Curtis Heaphy was trapped leg-before for 19 — to finish the day with 2 for 12, according to Cricbuzz. Dean Foxcroft, on 10 not out, and Zak Gibson, on 1 not out, saw out the last 26 balls to reach stumps at 36 for 2.

"Brief Scores: India A 464/5 decl. (Yashasvi Jaiswal 102, Sai Sudharsan 88, Tilak Varma 81*, Dhruv Jurel 71, Washington Sundar 50*; Zak Gibson 2-73) lead New Zealand A 36/2 (Prasidh Krishna 2-12) by 428 runs."

— Cricbuzz, day 2 report

What it means

This is an in-progress match, not a result. India A lead by 428 runs with New Zealand A's first innings barely begun, so the hosts must first avoid the follow-on conversation and then survive long enough on days 3 and 4 to keep the match alive. The fixture runs November 7-10 in Lincoln, according to CricTracker.

For India's selectors, the most closely watched name may be Prasidh. CricTracker noted his return comes ahead of the India Test series against New Zealand, which begins November 19, 2026. Two early wickets with the new ball, on return from a hamstring injury, is the kind of evidence that matters more than the size of the lead.

What's next

Play resumes on day 3 with New Zealand A at 36 for 2, still 428 runs behind. India A's route is straightforward: bowl the hosts out cheaply and close out a win inside four days. New Zealand A's first task is narrower — survive the first session.
